Subject: Acme Corp - Renewal & Expansion Recap (usage, pain points, next steps)

Hi Alex — thanks again for the time today. Below is a quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we’re all aligned. Let me know if I missed anything.

Call summary (major points)
- Current seat: Hosted API (pay-as-you-go). 6.2M embeddings tokens/month, peak 280 rps for search queries.
- Primary pain: latency spikes on search embedding lookups during peak hours and unpredictable token spend on high-volume OCR pipeline.
- New workloads: plan to launch a real-time semantic search for internal docs (higher QPS) and increase summarization usage for customer support.
- Goal for renewal: lock in predictable pricing and reduce unit cost while keeping 95th percentile latency under 120ms for embeddings.

Proposed upsell path
1) Short term (Q3 start): Dedicated capacity trial for embeddings (reserved pool sized for 500 rps) + prefix caching to reduce repeated token cost.
2) Mid term (Q3–Q4): Migrate semantic search to Dedicated; add 24/7 priority support and extended observability retention.
3) Contract: 12–18 month commitment with staged discounts tied to committed throughput.

Action items (owners & tentative timeline)
- Marissa: Share usage export + proposed pricing (attached) — today (attached).
- Rishi: Draft Dedicated sizing & committed throughput options — by Fri 6/12.
- Naomi: Outline onboarding plan and success metrics for a Q3 trial — by Mon 6/15.
- Alex / Acme: Share procurement timeline and any legal procurement constraints (PO/terms) — by Tue 6/16.

Attachments: usage_report_May2026.csv, proposed_pricing_ACME_Q3.pdf

Thanks again — excited to help reduce your unit costs and keep latency predictable.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Thanks Marissa — great recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 
1) The latency spikes seem to correlate to batch jobs running overnight (OCR ingest), not user-facing queries. Will a Dedicated pool help both workloads?
2) For procurement: Sarah (cc'd on this thread) runs procurement and will need an estimated annual spend to route through our purchasing system.

—Alex

Subject: Re: Acme Corp - Renewal & Expansion Recap (usage, pain points, next steps)

Hi Alex — good questions. Quick answers inline and next steps below.

> The latency spikes seem to correlate to batch jobs running overnight (OCR ingest), not user-facing queries. Will a Dedicated pool help both workloads?
Yes — Dedicated capacity lets you partition GPU pools by workload. We can provision a small reserved pool for realtime semantic search (low-latency, high-QPS) and a separate pool for batch OCR/ingest where throughput is optimized for cost. That avoids noisy-neighbor effects.

> For procurement: we need an estimated annual spend tied to throughput tiers.
Attached is a pricing matrix with three committed-throughput tiers (Conservative / Standard / Aggressive) and estimated annual spend for each. Conservative matches today's baseline + 15% buffer; Aggressive includes the planned search launch.

Notes on trial setup:
- Trial can be tunneled behind your current API endpoint (no DNS change) using our routing policy — zero-disruption.
- We'll set up an isolated tenant for the trial so logs/metrics stay separate.
- If you want, Marcus can scope the exact pool sizes after reviewing your CSV.

Next: I'll follow up with a sizing recommendation by EOD Fri 6/12.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Sales Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
[Attachment: proposed_pricing_ACME_Q3.pdf]

Hi Alex — quick note on onboarding and success metrics: 

Onboarding plan (Q3 trial):
- Week 0: Kickoff + access provisioning (we'll need a list of SAML/IDs).
- Week 1: Dedicated pool provisioning + routing (non-disruptive, behind existing endpoint).
- Week 2: Verification, load testing, and initial tuning (we'll run a smoke test with your OCR ingest sample).
- Week 3–4: Monitoring cadence and optimization; handover to your app team.

Success metrics (to evaluate the trial):
- Embedding 95th percentile latency <= 120ms under 95% of measured traffic patterns.
- Token cost reduction >= 20% versus current spend for the search workload.
- No production incidents or errors during trial window.

I can prepare a short onboarding checklist and estimated time per task — will share by Mon 6/15.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
